summary: BES-II hyperon spin observables lead the daily selection, supported by a quantum-rotor correction to nuclear-deformation inference, a synthesis of light-(hyper)nucleus production, a first but precision-limited PbPb charm dead-cone measurement, and two transferable learning methods for nuclear sensitivities and anomaly follow-up.
professional_summary: Hyperon global polarization, charm dead-cone jet substructure, quantum nuclear orientation, light-nucleus production mechanisms, gluon-saturation information geometry, active-subspace emulation, and representative anomaly confirmation define the selected literature.
strongest_paper_summary: arXiv:2611.03044 is the strongest result: STAR BES-II establishes Xi global polarization above 5 sigma in this energy range and finds 4.8 sigma evidence for increasing Lambda polarization with absolute rapidity.

papers.title: Global polarization of Lambda, Xi, and Omega hyperons in Au+Au collisions from the RHIC Beam Energy Scan-II
papers.abstract: STAR measures global polarization for strange and multistrange hyperons at seven BES-II energies. The data establish nonzero Lambda rapidity dependence and Xi polarization, constrain particle-antiparticle splitting, and map species and energy dependences relevant to vorticity and magnetic fields.
papers.summary: The study reports 4.8-sigma evidence that Lambda polarization rises with absolute rapidity and the first greater-than-5-sigma Xi polarization signal in this energy range, while finding no significant Lambda-antiparticle splitting.
papers.critical_assessment: The strongest paper today: very large samples, upgraded acceptance, two Xi extraction methods, and careful correlated systematics. Feed-down is uncorrected, low-energy models undershoot the data, and Omega interpretation remains dependent on its spin-transfer sign.

papers.title: Differential measurement of global polarization of Lambda, Xi, and Omega hyperons in Au+Au collisions at sqrt(sNN)=7.7-27 GeV from RHIC BES-II
papers.abstract: High-statistics BES-II data are used to measure centrality, transverse-momentum, and rapidity dependences of hyperon polarization. The centrality dependence is clear; other differential trends are small within current uncertainties.
papers.summary: Polarization rises toward peripheral events, with no significant pT dependence for Lambda or Xi and no significant Xi rapidity dependence at present precision.
papers.critical_assessment: A high-value companion measurement that sharply constrains spin transport. Null differential trends are sensitivity-limited constraints, and Omega precision remains insufficient for a firm species hierarchy.

papers.title: Probing the charm-quark dead cone effect in heavy ion collisions
papers.abstract: CMS measures late-kT hard-collinear emission angles for prompt-D0-tagged and inclusive jets in 5.02 TeV PbPb collisions. The flavor hierarchy resembles pp and disfavors large filling of the charm dead cone, but no significant medium-dependent change is resolved.
papers.summary: D0-tagged jets trend toward larger splitting angles than inclusive jets, while the PbPb-to-pp double ratio is compatible with unity.
papers.critical_assessment: Important and technically careful, but the equal-shape hypothesis is not excluded (p=0.16), the double ratio is compatible with unity (p=0.82), and present precision has little power to discriminate Hybrid from LIDO.

papers.title: Impact on Final-State Bulk Observables in Heavy-Ion Collisions from an Extended MC Glauber Model of Quantum Rotors
papers.abstract: An extended MC Glauber framework superposes nuclear orientations before collision sampling and propagates the resulting initial states through hydrodynamics and hadronic transport. Relative to classical rotors, quantum orientation reduces deformation-driven eccentricity and shifts several final-state flow observables.
papers.summary: Restoring rotational invariance suppresses ultra-central flow and moves deformation-sensitive correlations toward spherical-reference values, most strongly for Ne+Ne.
papers.critical_assessment: Strong targeted methodology with full final-state evolution. It is not a global fit, omits cluster correlations, and treats O and Au as spherical references, so it establishes a correction that matters rather than revised deformation parameters.

papers.title: Fisher-Rao Geometry of Gluon Saturation Fronts
papers.abstract: The paper defines a transverse Fisher-Rao metric for nonlinear saturation fronts after removing translation along the evolution flow. It derives rapid shape relaxation in Fisher-KPP and finds numerical evidence for corresponding behavior in BK evolution.
papers.summary: Information geometry separates front translation from shape memory and predicts a t^-4 relaxation of transverse distinguishability in the diffusive asymptotics.
papers.critical_assessment: Mathematically coherent and numerically checked, but not yet phenomenology: impact-parameter dependence, fitted uncertainties, and observable-level gains for EIC or heavy-ion inference remain to be demonstrated.

papers.title: Light nucleus and hypernucleus production at RHIC and LHC energies: a comparative study of phenomenological models
papers.short_authors: J. Aichelin, A. Andronic, F. Bellini, M. Bleicher, K. Blum, E. Bratkovskaya, et al.
papers.abstract: This EMMI task-force report reviews light-nucleus and hypernucleus data together with statistical, coalescence, kinetic, and transport descriptions. It emphasizes source sizes, wave functions, femtoscopy, formation dynamics, and measurements capable of separating mechanisms.
papers.summary: A broad theory-experiment synthesis maps model assumptions and identifies the differential and femtoscopic observables most likely to discriminate production mechanisms.
papers.critical_assessment: Authoritative and high-value as synthesis, but it is not a controlled global comparison and does not settle coalescence versus thermal or transport production.

papers.title: Active-subspace learning reveals dominant parameter directions in nuclear observables
papers.short_authors: Tom Plies, Margarida Companys Franzke, Achim Schwenk
papers.abstract: Active-subspace learning extracts low-dimensional combinations of chiral-EFT couplings directly from many-body calculations. These directions quantify global sensitivities and substantially improve Gaussian-process emulation for broad coupling variations.
papers.summary: More than 99% of gradient variation for several oxygen observables lies along one parameter direction, and active coordinates reduce the demonstrated calcium emulator error by over two orders of magnitude.
papers.critical_assessment: Strong, interpretable, and validated. Broader tests should address out-of-distribution behavior, emulator uncertainty calibration, neighbor-selection tuning, and the excluded unstable samples.

papers.title: Anomaly-ranked confirmation slows new-class learning
papers.abstract: Across five labeled benchmarks, anomaly detectors surface easy-to-recognize members of an unseen class that can nevertheless teach its full extent less efficiently than broader sampling. The study separates novelty discovery from representative confirmation.
papers.summary: In three systems, confirming the highest-ranked anomalies yields worse recognition than random within-class confirmation; classifier-driven selection recovers part of the loss.
papers.critical_assessment: Strong paired experiments and honest limitations. Withheld known classes, fixed representations, clean labels, and simplified confirmation costs mean a prospective collider study is still required.

cautions.title: Towards AI-Agent-Accelerated Research in High-Energy Physics: A Case Study in Monte Carlo Analysis
cautions.abstract: An LLM-assisted workflow reproduces benchmark values from a CEPC Monte Carlo analysis and performs an open-ended diagnosis of a muon-isolation effect under human supervision.
cautions.summary: The workflow reproduces four published detector-level points within about 2% and traces an isolation shift to angular efficiency and nearby hadronic activity.
cautions.critical_assessment: Useful feasibility evidence, but only one analysis, no formal blinding, no independent replication, and no controlled human-only baseline for time, errors, or intervention burden. It does not yet establish broad research acceleration.
